title: The Arithmetical Hierarchy and Post's Theorem

items.title: Bounded arithmetic formulas
items.strategy: Fix the language of arithmetic and define bounded quantifiers and bounded formulas, with primitive-recursive matrices as the base convention.

items.title: The classes Sigma_n^0, Pi_n^0, and Delta_n^0
items.strategy: Define levels by alternating unbounded quantifier blocks over a bounded matrix, and define Delta_n^0 by simultaneous membership.

items.title: Bounded quantifiers preserve primitive recursiveness
items.strategy: Replace bounded existential and universal tests by bounded primitive-recursive search and product constructions.

items.title: Sigma_1^0 sets are exactly the computably enumerable sets
items.strategy: Use Kleene normal form for the c.e.-to-Sigma_1 direction and bounded verification of a computation witness in the converse.

items.title: Delta_1^0 sets are exactly the decidable sets
items.strategy: Decide by dovetailing the two c.e. semideciders and use the complementary Sigma_1 characterization.

items.title: Prenex normalization preserves the arithmetical level
items.strategy: Push negations to the matrix and merge or pad quantifier blocks, recording the complement swap explicitly.

items.title: Completeness at an arithmetical level
items.strategy: Define Sigma_n^0- and Pi_n^0-completeness under total computable many-one reductions and keep the level parameter explicit.

items.title: The halting set is Sigma_1^0-complete
items.strategy: Express halting by a coded finite computation and reduce an arbitrary existential primitive-recursive predicate using an acceptable numbering.

items.title: The totality set is Pi_2^0-complete
items.strategy: Write totality as forall-input exists-stage verification and use s-m-n to compile a Pi_2 witness predicate into a program whose totality is equivalent to it.

items.title: Relative computability and relative enumerability
items.strategy: Define oracle-machine computation, A-computability, and A-c.e. sets using a fixed acceptable oracle programming convention.

items.title: An oracle computation has a finite query witness
items.strategy: Trace a halting oracle computation and isolate its finite query transcript; prove agreement of two oracles on that transcript preserves the run.

items.title: Post's theorem
items.strategy: Define finite jumps inside the statement, then prove the two inductions linking Sigma_{n+1}^0/Pi_{n+1}^0 to c.e.-in/co-c.e.-in 0^(n), using finite query witnesses for the reverse direction.

items.title: A diagonal set at each arithmetical level
items.strategy: For each finite jump, diagonalize against its oracle-c.e. enumeration and identify the resulting set through Post's theorem.

items.title: The arithmetical hierarchy is strict
items.strategy: Use the level-n diagonal set to separate adjacent Sigma and Pi levels, then derive all strict inclusions by monotonicity.

items.title: Limit-computable functions
items.strategy: Define pointwise convergence of a total computable approximation and distinguish convergence from a computably supplied modulus.

items.title: Shoenfield's limit lemma
items.strategy: Approximate a 0'-oracle computation by finite halting stages in one direction; in the other, decide eventual values with a 0' query about later changes.

items.title: False: Sigma_n^0 and Pi_n^0 are disjoint
items.strategy: Refute the claim with any decidable set, which belongs to both classes at every positive finite level.

items.title: False: a limit-computable function has a known stabilization stage
items.strategy: Show that a uniformly computable modulus for the standard halting approximation would decide the halting problem.

title: The Arithmetical Hierarchy and Post's Theorem: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Reading a c.e. definition as a Sigma_1^0 formula
items.strategy: Translate a concrete enumeration into an existential computation-witness formula and identify its level.

items.title: A limit approximation computed from the halting oracle
items.strategy: Work through the staged approximation to a 0'-computable characteristic function and identify why only eventual agreement is claimed.

items.title: A set lying in both Sigma_n^0 and Pi_n^0
items.strategy: Use a decidable set to give both presentations and contrast intersection with equality of the two classes.

items.title: An efficient universal simulation with a clock
items.strategy: Fix a multi-tape universal-machine convention, a self-delimiting program/input pairing, and an explicit clock; state the simulation overhead quantitatively.

items.title: Effective enumeration of clocked machines
items.strategy: Encode a machine together with a clock constructor and give total decoding, rejecting malformed encodings by a fixed default machine.

items.title: The time-diagonal language respects its budget
items.strategy: On an encoded clocked machine, reserve the constructible budget for parsing and universal simulation, and reject exactly when the simulation accepts before the clock expires.

items.title: The deterministic time hierarchy theorem
items.strategy: State the constructibility and logarithmic-overhead hypothesis explicitly, then use the budget-respecting diagonal language to obtain a proper DTIME containment.

items.title: P is properly contained in EXP
items.strategy: Apply time hierarchy with f(n)=2^ceil(sqrt(n)) and g(n)=2^n: f contains every polynomial and f log f=o(g).

items.title: The nondeterministic time hierarchy theorem
items.strategy: Use the alternating/guess-and-verify diagonal construction with its one-input-length slack, stating the exact constructibility and domination hypothesis.

items.title: Space-bounded universal simulation
items.strategy: Simulate a coded machine by storing only its active configuration and a constructible counter, with the program and input read from read-only tracks.

items.title: The space-diagonal machine halts
items.strategy: Bound configurations under the designated space cap and stop the diagonal simulation after the configuration bound, so looping runs cannot evade the construction.

items.title: The deterministic space hierarchy theorem
items.strategy: State the space-constructibility and asymptotic gap hypotheses and diagonalize using the forced-halting construction.

items.title: Read-only-input work-space classes and constructibility
items.strategy: Fix one read-only input tape and finitely many work tapes; define DWORKSPACE(s) by work cells only and work-space constructibility on unary input, and state the hierarchy-route floor s(n)>=ceil(log_2(n+2)) needed to address the input head, keeping this convention distinct from the earlier all-tapes DSPACE convention.

items.title: Universal simulation preserves read-only work space up to constants
items.strategy: Keep the encoded program and input on the read-only tape and store only the simulated finite control, work-tape contents, head positions, and an O(log n) input-head address; first obtain O(s(n)+log n) work space, then use the local logarithmic floor to obtain O(s(n)).

items.title: The read-only-workspace diagonal machine halts
items.strategy: Count the finitely many configurations permitted by the local work-space cap, stop the universal simulation at that bound, and show that the resulting diagonal machine halts while retaining the stated work-space budget.

items.title: The read-only-workspace space hierarchy theorem
items.strategy: For work-space-constructible f and g with ceil(log_2(n+2))=O(f(n)) and f=o(g), diagonalize the forced-halting local simulator to obtain DWORKSPACE(f) strictly contained in DWORKSPACE(g).

items.title: Read-only work space becomes all-tapes space after charging input
items.strategy: Regard the read-only input tape as an ordinary tape in the existing all-tapes model: on length n, its n input cells plus O(s(n)) work cells give DSPACE(n+s(n)).

items.title: L is properly contained in PSPACE
items.strategy: Use the standard local name L=DWORKSPACE(ceil(log_2(n+2))) and the read-only-workspace hierarchy at f(n)=ceil(log_2(n+2)), g(n)=n; charge the input through the bridge to place the separating DWORKSPACE(n) language in the existing all-tapes PSPACE.

items.title: Language padding
items.strategy: Define a canonical padded encoding x#1^m and the associated padded language, including malformed-string convention.

items.title: Padding transfers time bounds
items.strategy: Give both directions of the padding translation and account for construction and decoding time in terms of the padded input length.

items.title: Gap and union theorems for abstract complexity bounds
items.strategy: State the precise conditional versions for an abstract Blum complexity measure and a uniformly recursive bound family, defining the class notation in the statement before proving the gap and union constructions.

items.title: Hierarchy theorems do not separate P from NP
items.strategy: Compare the quantified class separations supplied by the hierarchy theorems with the particular P-versus-NP question; no claim about its truth value is inferred.

items.title: False: unrestricted diagonalization respects any resource bound
items.strategy: Refute the assertion by exposing parsing, universal-simulation, and constructibility overhead that the clocked construction must reserve.

title: Time and Space Hierarchy Theorems: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Budgeting a time-diagonal language
items.strategy: Trace a valid clocked input through parsing, simulation, and complementing, showing where the time reserve is spent.

items.title: Why a hierarchy separation is not a P versus NP separation
items.strategy: Compare the two quantified statements on a concrete pair of time bounds and identify the missing P-versus-NP implication.

items.title: Overhead breaks an unrestricted diagonalization claim
items.strategy: Exhibit a valid one-step computation whose complete self-delimiting decoding already exceeds the claimed one-step simulator budget.
